notes:
GAMbit now reads your own custom schemas, so you can look up users in an org unit and the CSV export includes your fields.

If Read schemas from Google comes back empty, use Learn from this person instead.

Set it up once: go to Settings & Updates → Custom user fields, or click Custom fields… on Users → Find users.

Read schemas from Google lists every schema and field you have, such as Student_Information → Student_ID, Grade, Current_School.
If your admin role can’t read schemas, type a student who has the fields filled in and click Learn from this person.
Tick the fields you want and set their order with Move up / Move down.
Choose how the columns are named:
Friendly: Grade, Student ID.
GAM style: Student_Information.Grade, which you can edit and send straight back to GAM to update users.
If you’ve set a team folder, every tech gets the same fields. The setting is also included in the deployment file.

Where the fields appear:

Lists: they’re added as columns to Users → Find users (including “In org unit(s)”), Org units → users, and Reports → Inactive accounts. Export CSV and Google Sheet include them, one column per field.
Lookup: the student card shows them, e.g. “Student ID 001x48x9x · Grade 7th Grade”.
Search: Users → Find users → Show Custom field. Pick a field, then is / contains / starts with / is empty / has a value, and optionally limit it to org units.
For example: Grade is “7th Grade” in /Students/Middle School, then export.
Exact matches on searchable fields go straight to Google. Other searches, like “contains”, load the users first and check each one, so limit them to an org unit for speed.
